messages.content:
The `getParsedOptionValue` method in the `CommandLine` class retrieves the parsed value of a specified option. It first gets the option value as a string and then resolves the corresponding option. If either the option is null or the value is null, it returns null. Otherwise, it creates and returns a value based on the option's type.

Looking at the `Option` class constructor with the signature `Option(String opt, String description)`, it takes in an option name and description. The issue described in the current bug report is that the user expects the default type of an option to be a String unless explicitly set to any other type. However, in the `Option` constructor shown, there is no explicit setting of the type. 

Based on the failing test `testGetParsedOptionValue`, the user adds an option with a number type for option `-i` and a default type for option `-f`. When parsing the command line with values for these options, the user expects the parsed value of option `-f` (which has no explicit type set) to be returned as a String, but it returns null as the type is not set.

To address this issue, the default type for an option when not explicitly set could be modified to default to String. This can be achieved by updating the `Option` constructor to set the type to String by default if not specified.

Therefore, the root cause of the issue is that the default type for an option is not being explicitly set to String when not specified, leading to unexpected behavior when retrieving parsed option values.

Next, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to address this bug.
```
org.apache.commons.cli.Option.Option(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)
```

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
